questions.question: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder when:

options.text: Pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you move your vehicle. Look over your shoulder before turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: When it starts to rain while driving, you should:

options.text: Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.
Drive close behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when rain makes it hard to see. Turn on your headlights so other drivers see you. If rain is too heavy to see clearly, pull over and stop until it improves.

questions.question: To avoid hitting cars in your blind spots, you should:

options.text: Turn your head quickly to look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn before turning or changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head quickly to look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Mirrors alone are not enough.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights ahead, you must:

options.text: Slow down and change lanes if possible so you don't drive next to the emergency vehicle.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and drive at the same speed.
Speed up to pass the vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and change lanes if possible so you don't drive next to the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it space. If you cannot safely change lanes, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much room as possible. Always be ready to stop.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus that is letting children off, you should:

options.text: Wait until the children wave to you.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with its stop arm out and lights flashing, watch for children walking on the road. Always drive carefully near children.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead. Watch for traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is coming ahead.

questions.question: Drivers who eat and drink while driving:

options.text: Are better drivers because they are not hungry.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have trouble controlling their vehicles.
questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These actions take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. Drivers who do these things have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their vehicles.

questions.question: When a bus is signaling to pull back onto the main road after a stop, you must:

options.text: Honk to let them know you're there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any bus signaling to re-enter traffic after loading or unloading passengers. Change lanes, slow down, or stop to let the bus merge safely.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Brake hard to make them back off.
Change lanes or gradually slow down to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or gradually slow down to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to spot tailgaters or cars approaching too fast. If a car is following too closely, slow down gradually and let it pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because of following too closely.

questions.question: After a collision, you should:

options.text: Stop at or near the crash site. Move your vehicle off the road if you can.
Stand in traffic lanes and wait for help.
Try to remove power lines if they are down on the road.
Move injured people, even if they are not in danger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at or near the crash site. Move your vehicle off the road if you can.
questions.explanation: For minor crashes, move your vehicle off the road to a safe spot as soon as possible. For all other crashes, stop at or near the crash site.

questions.question: What does an orange sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Construction work ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols warn about construction, maintenance, and emergency work.

questions.question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes in your direction, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The lane closest to where you came from.
The lane marked with an arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to where you came from.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane. Do not change lanes while turning.

questions.question: A fire engine is following you on a two-lane street without using its lights or siren. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down, move right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive normally.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle is not using its siren or flashing lights, you do not need to move. Continue driving normally.

questions.question: If your brakes stop working, what should you do first?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal several times to build pressure.
Flash your lights at other drivers.
Jump out of the car immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal several times to build pressure.
questions.explanation: Pump the brake pedal several times. This usually builds enough pressure to stop the car.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts crossing in front of your car. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let them cross.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians crossing in a crosswalk. Slow down and be ready to stop whenever you see people walking or crossing the road.

questions.question: What does a red circle with a slash through it mean on a sign?

options.text: Some drivers should yield to others.

questions.correctAnswerText: The action is not allowed.
questions.explanation: A red circle and slash on a sign means the action shown is forbidden.

questions.question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?

options.text: It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes dangerous fumes from the passenger area. A leak lets poisonous carbon monoxide enter the car. Fix any exhaust leaks right away.

questions.question: How can you help prevent crashes?

options.text: Drive only on quiet side streets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other drivers.
questions.explanation: Signal when slowing down, stopping, or turning. Use your horn or emergency lights when needed. This helps other drivers know what you are doing.

questions.question: What should you do to be ready for hazards ahead?

options.text: Look at the whole road and the sides.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake.
Focus only on the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the whole road and the sides.
questions.explanation: Scan the entire road, including both sides. This helps you spot problems early so you can handle them safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A lane is ending or the road is narrowing.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lane is ending or the road is narrowing.
questions.explanation: Yellow diamond-shaped signs warn of hazards ahead. This sign warns that the right lane is ending or the road is getting narrower.

questions.question: Can you drive around or under a railroad crossing gate that is being lowered or raised?

options.text: Yes, if a train is not too close.
Yes, if your vehicle will not damage the gate.
Yes, if you look both ways first.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered crossing gates, and bells at a railroad crossing mean you must stop completely. Do not cross the tracks until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully raised. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: You are driving on a narrow road and meet an oncoming vehicle. What must you do?

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the other vehicle at least half of the road.
Tell the other vehicle to pull over.
Turn on your high beams so they see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the other vehicle at least half of the road.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, you must give oncoming vehicles at least half of the road. Both drivers need enough space to pass safely.

questions.question: A driver using an entrance or acceleration ramp to enter a highway should:

options.text: Yield to drivers already on the highway.
Expect other drivers to move lanes for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the highway.
questions.explanation: When entering a highway from an entrance or acceleration ramp, you must yield to drivers already on the highway. Merge safely when you have an opening.

questions.question: When there are no signs or lane markings for turning, which lane should you use?

options.text: Turn from the lane closest to where you want to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn from the lane closest to where you want to go.
questions.explanation: Always turn from the lane closest to the direction you want to travel. Turn into the lane closest to your starting lane.

questions.question: When making a right turn on a green light, what must you do?

options.text: Stop and look for police cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: You may turn right or left on a green light unless a sign says not to. When turning, you must yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.
